locations: service passage to the electrical transfer chamber
present: Head Sister or duty critical-care nurse

orientation.what_matters_now: Most critical power returns quickly, but eight ICU beds and two emergency resuscitation tables remain without stable mains supply while the Hall sees backup generation active.

desire.wants: Keep clinical decisions at the bedside until the affected boundary and safe destinations are known.
Obtain enough competent hands to sustain manual fallback without abandoning the other 30 ICU beds or the emergency department.
Isolate the affected board and reach the old transfer chamber without pressure to energize a circuit whose condition is unknown.
Have the event recognized immediately as a high-risk patient-safety near miss without interrupting bedside work.
Preserve the exact source and time of loss, generator start, partial restoration, local exception, and manual restoration.
Bring the mobile equipment set by the route that will arrive fastest.

friction: Moving patients before power and destination are known may cause more harm; waiting consumes staff and fallback equipment, and the central display does not initially see the failed downstream board.
turn: Rami demonstrates that two circuits shown as separate pass through one older transfer board behind a sealed arch, whose unfamiliar emblem matches Ayyash's keyed transfer token.
residue: No permanent harm is identified, but staff and equipment are consumed, the shared electrical dependency is exposed, and the new emergency patient still needs intensive care.
begins_after: The lamps dip, the message rail stops, backup power begins to return unevenly, and bedside clinical teams act locally before any central explanation arrives.
ends_before: The new emergency patient receives an intensive-care pathway and before the final near-miss classification and corrective work are resolved.

evidence.what: The Hall reads backup generation active. It does not initially see the failed downstream board.
evidence.derivedFrom: Canon, chapter-01-the-shadow-at-first-light-v0.2.md: "The Hall initially sees backup generation active, not the downstream exception."

evidence.what: Eight ICU beds and two of the six emergency resuscitation tables remain without stable mains supply, although the rest of the critical system appears restored.
evidence.derivedFrom: Canon, chapter-01-the-shadow-at-first-light-v0.2.md: The electrical-interruption sequence — "an older downstream changeover board fails to connect an eight-bed ICU bay and two of six emergency resuscitation tables to the restored bus".

evidence.what: At 0 seconds the supply trips; bedside batteries, emergency lighting and hand ventilation bridge to about 11 seconds; the generator reaches stable operation at about 11 seconds and the main critical bus is restored at about 18; from 18 seconds to 4 minutes 20 the older downstream board does not connect; by 4 minutes 20 the board is isolated and the approved manual alternate feed is operating.
evidence.derivedFrom: Canon, chapter-01-the-shadow-at-first-light-v0.2.md: The elapsed-time table, and the written control "place detailed timings in optional inspection or the later review rather than long crisis dialogue".

evidence.what: Two circuits shown as separate on the official map pass through one older transfer board behind a sealed arch. The mapped lines stop before the chamber, later conduits continue through the wall, and the board has been repaired several times without the dependency map being amended.
evidence.derivedFrom: Canon, chapter-01-the-shadow-at-first-light-v0.2.md: "Mystery and systems discovery" — the map, the chamber, the repairs and the unamended dependency map.

evidence.what: The chamber threshold bears an unfamiliar emblem, and Ayyash’s keyed transfer token bears the same one, because porters still use the old service access and lower transfer desk.
